correctness.rationale: The allowed leading halves count as F_(h-1) for length 2h (last digit forced zero), and F_h+F_(h-1) for 2h+1 (the second count allows a central one). Fibonacci parity is symmetric under negation modulo 3, making all mirror pairs and the possible center even when 3 divides L. For the other two congruences the signed weights after the forced leading bit give the three-step matrix products diag(-1,1) and [[1,2],[0,-1]], respectively. Both square to identity, so six more half-positions give the same signed sum, with unchanged center sign; the L=1,2 seeds agree with L=13,14. For L>=13 the endpoint word and each individual extra mirror pair at index k=4,5,6,7 are admissible: the extra bits are at least two indices from each other and from the endpoints. Subtracting the endpoint value gives P_k=F_k+F_(L+3-k). The two consecutive reverse-Fibonacci cancellations give -10 and -16, so the common gcd divides 2. Off resonance an odd value is the endpoint value for L=2 mod 3, or the endpoint value plus P_4 for L=1 mod 3. The independent finite replay enumerated 28,655 words for L=1..40, including all exceptional gcds and the empty L=2 family, with the claimed counts and table. The recurrence and witnesses, not the enumeration, establish all lengths.
residual_risks: Finite replay is bounded; this is a mathematical review, not a formal proof certificate.

value.rationale: Length is the natural shell for canonical Fibonacci representations. The result distinguishes complete parity resonance from bounded even/odd discrepancies, and settles whether all values in each shell have any common divisor at all. Uniform gcd witnesses and the full exceptional range give exact usable information not supplied by a list of examples.
residual_risks: No classification of individual residues beyond parity or claims for other numeration systems.
